chunks: 3428 - Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

That ʿAlī عليه السلام was in the Masjid of Kūfah, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Qufl al-Taymī passed by him carrying Ṭalḥah's coat of mail. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “This is Ṭalḥah's coat of mail; it was taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah.” Ibn Qufl said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, appoint between me and yourself the judge whom you have approved for the Muslims.” So he appointed Shurayḥ between him and him. Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “This is Ṭalḥah's coat of mail; it was taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah.” Shurayḥ said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, bring proof for what you say.”

So he brought to him al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, and he testified that it was Ṭalḥah's coat of mail, taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah. Shurayḥ said: “This is one witness, and I do not judge by one witness unless another is with him.” Then he brought Qanbar, and he testified that it was Ṭalḥah's coat of mail, taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah. He said: “This is a slave, and I do not judge by the testimony of a slave.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام became angry and said: “Take the coat of mail, for this one has judged unjustly three times.” So Shurayḥ moved away from his seat and said: “I will not judge between two people until you inform me from where I judged unjustly three times.”

So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him: “When I told you that it was Ṭalḥah's coat of mail, taken as ghulūl on the day of Baṣrah, you said: ‘Bring proof for what you say,’ though the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘Wherever ghulūl is found, it is taken without proof.’ So I said: ‘A man who has not heard the hadith.’ Then I brought you al-Ḥasan and he testified, but you said: ‘This is one witness, and I do not judge by one witness unless another is with him,’ while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم judged by one witness and an oath; so those are two. Then I brought you Qanbar and he testified, but you said: ‘This is a slave,’ while there is no harm in the testimony of a slave when he is just; so this is the third.”

Then he عليه السلام said: “O Shurayḥ, the Imam of the Muslims is entrusted in their affairs with what is greater than this.” Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “So the first one who rejected the testimony of the slave was Rumaʿ.”

key_terms.إِمَامَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the divinely authoritative leader entrusted with the affairs of the Muslims
key_terms.بِجَوْرٍ: with injustice or an unjust ruling
key_terms.غُلُولاً: property taken unlawfully from war spoils
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: an enslaved person whose testimony is discussed here
key_terms.يَمِينٍ: an oath used together with testimony in judgment

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام correct Shurayḥ’s judicial errors in the case of Ṭalḥah’s armor?
ai.summary: This report recounts a judicial dispute in which Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام corrects Shurayḥ’s rulings regarding evidentiary standards, the use of a single witness with an oath, and the acceptance of a just slave’s testimony. It also highlights the authority and trust vested in the Imam of the Muslims in matters of public concern and legal judgment.
